title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck studies outer automorphisms u of the profinite loop group Π̂_{0,3} (fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}) that commute, in the outer sense, with the S_3 symmetries. These are the generators σ_∞ (order 2) and ρ (order 3), and μ ∈ Ẑ^* is the multiplier of u, essentially the cyclotomic character. Such a u extends to the extension Ŝ^+_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z)^∧' and then descends to the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ)'. The goal, stated on the next page as Theorem (75)-(78) and its Corollary, is to show that the descended action is conjugation by an explicit matrix u̲ ∈ GL(2,Ẑ) with det u̲ = μ.

The matrices. Take σ_∞ = [[0,1],[-1,0]] and ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]], so ρ^{-1} = [[1,-1],[1,0]]. Matrices commuting with σ_∞ have the form tσ_∞ + u = [[u,t],[-t,u]], a 'Gaussian integer' u+it. Its determinant is u^2 + t^2, which is fixed to equal ε_2/μ.

The sign ε_2. Here ε_2 = ±1 according as μ ≡ ±1 (mod 4). This is forced 2-adically, since a unit of Z_2 is a sum of two squares only if it is ≡ 1 mod 4.

Previous page. Case ε_2 = +1: u̲ = μ(tσ_∞ + u) is a similitude with det μ, and [u̲, ρ] = g, where g is the element given by formula (65).

This page, case ε_2 = -1. Here one expects an antisimilitude (u̲^t u̲ = -det u̲ · Id).
- First trial: u̲ = μ[[u,t],[t,-u]]. Then u̲^t u̲ = μ^2(u^2+t^2) Id = -μ Id and det u̲ = -μ^2(u^2+t^2) = μ, using u^2+t^2 = -1/μ.
- Commutator: [u̲, ρ] = u̲ρu̲^{-1}ρ^{-1}, with u̲^{-1} = [[-u,-t],[-t,u]]. The partial products are [[-t,u+t],[u,t-u]] and [[-u-t,u],[u-t,t]]. The result is [u̲,ρ] = [[μu(u+t), μt^2],[1-μu(u-t), -1-μut]]. I verified all entries.
- Comparing with -g from (65) gives the spurious condition 2μut = 0, i.e. ut = 0 ('décidément, ça déconne!').
- Diagnosis: t had the wrong sign. The correct choice is u̲ = μ(tσ_∞ + u)τ_∞ = μ[[u,-t],[-t,-u]], still an antisimilitude of determinant μ. With it, [u̲,ρ] = -g.

Next page. This yields the uniform formula u̲ = μ(tσ_∞+u)τ_∞^{α_2}, with det u̲ = μ, u̲σ_∞u̲^{-1} = ε_2 σ_∞ and [u̲,ρ] = ε_2 g. The Corollary: the action of any such automorphism on the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ)' is inner from GL(2,Ẑ), by a matrix of determinant μ.

In modern terms, this is an explicit normalizer computation showing that GT-type automorphisms (or Galois elements) act on the congruence completion of SL_2 through the cyclotomic character, via an explicit element of the normalizer in GL_2(Ẑ) of the image of the S_3 torsion.
errors: The first ansatz u̲ = μ[[u,t],[t,-u]] gives the wrong sign of t; Grothendieck detects this himself through the inconsistent condition ut = 0 and corrects it.

In the corrected formula for [u̲,ρ], the (1,1) entry should be μu(u-t), not μu(u+t). This follows from replacing t by -t in the first computation, and the next page indeed checks μu(u-t) = -(1+μt(t-u)). This is either a slip in the manuscript or a misreading.

The (2,1) entry of the corrected commutator, 1-μu(u+t), can only be checked against the explicit form of g in (65), which is not on this page. Taking the ε_2 = +1 form of g from the previous page, the (2,1) entries would not match. So g in (65) presumably has a different sign pattern in the ε_2 = -1 case; this cannot be verified here.

ideas.what: Parametrizing the centralizer of σ_∞ in GL_2(Ẑ) as 'Gaussian integers' u + tσ_∞, with norm u^2+t^2 = ±1/μ. For μ ≡ -1 mod 4, the reflection τ_∞ is needed, giving an antisimilitude.
ideas.modern_name: Normalizer of the finite (S_3 / order-4 torsion) subgroup in GL_2(Ẑ); 2-adic sums of two squares

ideas.what: Automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3} commuting with S_3 (GT-type elements) induce on the congruence completion SL(2,Ẑ) an action that is inner from GL(2,Ẑ), by a matrix of determinant equal to the multiplier μ (cyclotomic character).
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT / Gal(Q̄/Q) on the congruence completion of SL_2(Z) factors through the cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps in the GT setting (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the GT-like group and SL_2 informally; no explicit matrix formula is known to me

ideas.what: Checking the outer S_3-equivariance via the commutator identities [u̲,σ_∞] = ε_2 and [u̲,ρ] = ε_2 g (g ∈ Π).
ideas.modern_name: Normalization conditions analogous to Drinfeld's GT relations (f(x,y)f(y,x)=1, hexagon) written in matrix form

missed.claim: Explicit formula u̲ = μ(tσ_∞+u)τ_∞^{α_2}, with μ(u^2+t^2) = ε_2, for the GL_2(Ẑ)-matrix by which an S_3-commuting automorphism of Π̂_{0,3} acts on SL(2,Ẑ). The sign ε_2 = ±1 is determined by μ mod 4, giving a similitude or an antisimilitude.
missed.quote: je vois que j'ai remplacé dans la définition de u t par -t, i.e. j'ai défini u̲ = μ(tσ_∞ + u)τ_∞
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete early (pre-Drinfeld) normalization of the cyclotomic-character action of GT-type automorphisms on the congruence completion. The underlying fact is well known; the explicit S_3-adapted matrix choice is a minor historical detail.

deep.surprise_reason: This is mainly a routine matrix verification with a self-corrected sign error. The underlying result, that the action on SL(2,Ẑ) is inner by a determinant-μ element, is folklore in the GT literature. Only the explicit S_3-adapted parametrization with the mod-4 dichotomy is a small unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: The first line reads 'convaincra' (continuing 'je prévois que la matrice ... convaincra'), preceded by the page number 368.
In the final displayed commutator, the (1,1) entry should mathematically be μu(u-t); the manuscript or transcription shows μu(u+t).
In the first commutator, the bracket under the first product should read [[-t, u+t],[u, -u+t]], which matches the transcription.
